title: GS-KAN shared parent function with Mirror edge Views
hypothesis: Compositional Mirror edge Views over one shared GS-KAN parent function represent heldout scalar edge functions with fewer complete bytes or lower evaluation work than native GS-KAN affine transforms and independent KAN edge functions.

world.view: f(a*x+b), with per-edge affine codes and optional bounded modulation

fresh.release_rule: Keep fresh sealed after native GS-KAN exact alias or failure of complete-byte/compute gate.

metrics: full serialized bytes including parent and codes
success_gate: heldout nRMSE <=0.02, at least 25% fewer complete bytes than native GS-KAN and independent control, and strict function/evaluation frontier gain over native affine GS-KAN.
failure_gate: FAIL if native GS-KAN affine transformation exactly matches Mirror or complete bytes/compute do not improve.
boundaries: Synthetic analytic scalar edge functions only; no trained KAN claim.
The parent function and transforms are known; heldout edge parameters are included in payload.
No fresh samples after native alias or gate failure.
